tagline: Social Security does not ask whether you are sick. It asks whether you can do any job that exists in significant numbers in the national economy. For a Southfield claimant whose career was at a desk, that is a harder question than it sounds, and the claim is built around it.
primaryKeyword: social security disability attorney southfield (70/mo) · southfield social security disability lawyer (40/mo)

c.v: About two in three first applications for Social Security Disability are denied, and many of the people denied are in fact disabled. They are denied because the application did not answer the question Social Security actually asks: not “are you sick?” but “can you do any job that exists in significant numbers in the national economy, given your age, education, and work history?” For a Southfield claimant, the answer often turns on what kind of work they did. Southfield is an office city: insurance, health care administration, engineering, auto supplier offices, and call centers along Northwestern Highway, Telegraph, and the Town Center. A claimant whose past work was sedentary has a harder path at the last two steps of the test than one who did heavy labor, because Social Security will ask whether they can still do a desk job. Winning that claim means proving, with medical evidence, why they cannot.

c.v: Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)

is for people who worked and paid Social Security taxes: generally 40 work credits, 20 of them in the ten years before disability, fewer for younger workers. The benefit is based on your earnings record, with Medicare after 24 months of entitlement. Because the benefit tracks earnings, a Southfield professional with a long, well-paid career often has a substantial SSDI benefit, and the back pay matters accordingly. See our
SSDI page
Supplemental Security Income (SSI)

is for people with little income and few assets, whether or not they worked: $994 a month for an individual in 2026 and $1,029 in 2027, reduced by other income, with a $2,000 asset limit (home and one vehicle excluded) and Michigan Medicaid. Some claimants qualify for both. See our
SSI page

sections.heading: The five-step test, as it applies to a Southfield claim

c.v: Social Security uses a five-step sequential evaluation (20 CFR 404.1520), deciding the claim at the first step where the answer is clear.
Are you working above the substantial gainful activity level?

items.v: Earning more than $1,690 a month in 2026 ($1,770 in 2027) generally ends the claim at step one. Part-time or accommodated work below that level does not.

c.v: Is your impairment severe and expected to last 12 months or result in death?

items.v: A diagnosis is not enough; the record must show functional limits.

c.v: Does your condition meet or equal a Listing?

items.v: Meeting one wins the claim here. See our

Can you do your past relevant work?

items.v: Social Security assesses your residual functional capacity (RFC), what you can still do despite your limitations, and compares it to the jobs you held in the past five years.

c.v: five-year relevant-work period under the 2024 rule

items.v: If you did a desk job, a physical limitation alone may not end your ability to do it. The claim then depends on limits that affect any job: the need to lie down or take unscheduled breaks, absences from treatment or flare-ups, the inability to sit for long periods, limits on using the hands for typing, or concentration and memory deficits from pain, medication, or a mental health condition.

c.v: Can you do any other work?

items.v: Using your RFC, age, education, and work experience under the Medical-Vocational Guidelines (the “grids”). Age matters: at 50 and above, the grids favor claimants limited to sedentary work who cannot transfer their skills. Skilled office work can produce transferable skills, so the vocational evidence about what your skills were, and whether they transfer to other sedentary work, is often contested at the hearing.

sections.heading: Where the evidence comes from in Southfield

c.v: The claim is the record. We obtain and organize it from every source: Henry Ford Providence Southfield Hospital (formerly Ascension Providence) and its clinics; Corewell Health William Beaumont University Hospital in Royal Oak; DMC Sinai-Grace Hospital; the physician and specialist offices along Northwestern Highway, Twelve Mile, and Telegraph; mental health providers, including those in the Oakland Community Health Network, Oakland County’s public mental health system, which are often the core of a claim and the hardest records to obtain; the John D. Dingell VA Medical Center for veterans; and the consultative examination ordered by Michigan’s Disability Determination Services, which a claimant should attend but should never rely on.
provider list wording

A treating provider’s opinion on your specific functional limits, in a form the regulations recognize (20 CFR 404.1520c), is often the difference at the hearing. Your employer’s records also count: performance reviews, accommodation requests, and FMLA leave can show how the condition affected your work before you stopped.

c.v: Hearings for Southfield claimants are often scheduled by the Oak Park hearing office at 25900 Greenfield Road, though the assignment follows the field office handling the claim and can be Detroit or Livonia; hearings are in person, by video, or by phone, and you may ask to appear in person. Missing a 60-day deadline usually means starting over with a new application and can cost back pay. Appeal; do not reapply.
Looking for the Social Security office?

You do not have to visit an office to apply or appeal: both can be done online at ssa.gov or by calling Social Security’s national number. If you want in-person help, SSA’s office locator gives the field office assigned to your ZIP code.

SSDI benefits begin five full months after the established onset date; SSI is not paid for months before the application. SSDI back pay reaches to the onset date, up to 12 months before the application, and the onset date your lawyer proves sets the amount. The fee is set by federal law: 25 percent of back benefits, capped at the current limit, and nothing if the claim is not approved (42 USC 406(a)). Social Security pays it directly from back pay; ongoing monthly benefits are not subject to it.

sections.heading: How a Southfield disability claim interacts with other claims

c.v: An employer’s long-term disability plan.

items.v: Many Southfield office employers provide group LTD insurance. Many plans require you to apply for SSDI, offset the SSDI award dollar for dollar, and may claim repayment from your SSDI back pay. An LTD denial has its own 180-day ERISA appeal deadline (29 CFR 2560.503-1), and the LTD file and the Social Security file should tell the same story.

faqs.question: I had a desk job. Can I still get disability?

answer.v: Yes, if the medical evidence shows you cannot sustain even sedentary work, for example because of the need for unscheduled breaks, frequent absences, limits on sitting or on using your hands, or problems with concentration. Age 50 and above changes the analysis in your favor if your skills do not transfer.

faqs.question: My employer’s long-term disability insurer told me to apply for Social Security. Why?

answer.v: Because many LTD plans reduce your LTD benefit by the SSDI award and may ask you to repay overlapping months from your back pay. Read the plan before you sign a repayment agreement, and make sure both claims describe your limits the same way.

faqs.question: How long do I have to appeal?

answer.v: Sixty days from the date on the denial notice, plus five days for mailing, at every stage.
Often through the Oak Park hearing office, though it can be Detroit or Livonia; in person, by video, or by phone. You can ask to appear in person.
From January 2027, the SGA limit rises to $1,770 a month, the trial work month to $1,270, and the SSI federal benefit to $1,029 for an individual, with a 3.6 percent increase in benefits.
